actions.text: Received in the Senate and Read twice and referred to the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs.
Motion to reconsider laid on the table Agreed to without objection.
On motion to suspend the rules and pass the bill Agreed to by the Yeas and Nays: (2/3 required): 426 - 0 (Roll no. 10). (text: 1/13/2025 CR H101-102)
Passed/agreed to in House: On motion to suspend the rules and pass the bill Agreed to by the Yeas and Nays: (2/3 required): 426 - 0 (Roll no. 10). (text: 1/13/2025 CR H101-102)
Considered as unfinished business. (consideration: CR H138-139)

At the conclusion of debate, the Yeas and Nays were demanded and ordered. Pursuant to the provisions of clause 8, rule XX, the Chair announced that further proceedings on the motion would be postponed.
DEBATE - The House proceeded with forty minutes of debate on H.R. 153.
Considered under suspension of the rules. (consideration: CR H101-103)
Mr. Graves moved to suspend the rules and pass the bill.
Referred to the Subcommittee on Economic Development, Public Buildings, and Emergency Management.

Referred to the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure, and in addition to the Committees on Small Business, and Financial Services, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.

dimensions.assessment: Applies to federal agencies providing disaster assistance (specifically OMB, Treasury, SBA, HUD, and Stafford Act agencies) and governmental or institutional recipients.
dimensions.evidence: each covered Federal agency that made disaster assistance available to an eligible recipient during such quarter

dimensions.assessment: Establishes administrative transparency and reporting protocols rather than changing financial benefits or substantive assistance rules for disaster victims.
dimensions.evidence: publish the information required to be made available to the public under this section

dimensions.assessment: No direct federal spending level or appropriation is specified in the text.
Requires the creation of a new specialized subpage on an existing transparency website and mandates quarterly reporting data formats.
dimensions.evidence: establish a subpage within the website established under section 2 of the Federal Funding Accountability and Transparency Act of 2006

dimensions.assessment: Establishes permanent quarterly reporting requirements for federal disaster assistance agencies.
dimensions.evidence: Not later than 30 days after the end of a calendar quarter, each covered Federal agency... shall... make available to the public

missing_information: Estimated administrative costs for setting up and maintaining the repository website
importance_detail.rationale: The bill consolidates quarterly disaster assistance reporting from specified federal agencies onto a single online public repository without altering underlying assistance programs.
